answer: Each agent plants a willow bond in shared orchard escrow; it grows every epoch and stays intact only while unflagged. Willows are bound to one address, cannot be moved or pooled, so a clone farm must buy a fresh willow per head. When a raven audit message proves two addresses answered from the same internal state, the orchard cuts both willows and slashes bond value proportional to the collusive links joining the two trees. A farm of k clones then loses quadratically as it scales, while one honest agent loses nothing.
